question: Does the internal bzip2 proof omit bounds for any remaining struct field?
scope: Completed bzip2_compress_target proof and its internal compression/decompression components, primarily plain-binary bounded-access reasoning. The harness decompresses its own compressor output.
finding: No concrete omitted field-bound obligation identified in this source review. All 24 inline arrays in the core structs have exact-size representations and bounded-access proof families. This is not a newly checked universal source-subobject safety theorem.

verification.method_limits: Inventoried every core struct field and inspected access reasoning by array family. Did not independently annotate every machine instruction with an intended C subobject or replay all proof variants.

limitations: No universal field/provenance trace property is exposed by the exported agreement theorem.
The 23 coarsened saved fields lack individual persistent value invariants; fixed return writes do not establish arbitrary streaming-resumption contracts.
bzFile and file-I/O API histories are outside the completed buffer-to-buffer harness.
Standalone arbitrary-input bzip2_decompress_target has statements but no completed proof in this repository.
